=== MITIGATION INVENTORY (Layer 3a / D4) — NON-TEST ===
Directive : D4 (Layer 3a - Mitigation Inventory).  Mode: DETERMINISTIC.  Read-only (modifies NO source files).
Purpose   : 100%-recall enumeration of EXISTING DEFENSIVE controls across the 9 mitigation categories over
            first-party NON-TEST source files. Layer 3b (taint) cross-references this inventory to decide
            whether a sink finding has a "validated mitigation on the path" (which downgrades it from
            gateBlocking:true to advisory). This file asserts NO exploitability by itself.
Repository: calcom-monorepo (blitzy-cal)
Method    : deterministic `grep -HInE "<pattern>"` sweep, one pass per category, over the NON-TEST file set;
            output ANSI-stripped, CR-stripped, left-trimmed, snippet truncated to 200 chars, secret-redacted,
            then `LC_ALL=C sort -t: -k1,1 -k2,2n` (by file path, then numeric line). Re-running on identical
            repository content yields byte-identical output (reproducibility anchor for a deterministic layer).

scope        : first-party source files with extensions: .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .cjs
exclude_dirs : node_modules .yarn .next dist build .turbo coverage .git
test-exclusion (these are TEST files; routed to mitigation-inventory-test.txt and NOT listed here):
   (a) spec-convention basenames (delimited by start | '.' | '-' | '/'):
         *.test.<ext>  *.spec.<ext>  *.e2e.<ext>  *.e2e-spec.<ext>  *.integration-test.<ext>
         (also a bare test.<ext> / spec.<ext> / *-test.<ext>)
   (b) test-data / mock / fixture / storybook basenames: *.mock.<ext>  *.fixture.<ext>  *.stories.<ext>
   (c) test config/setup/util basenames: setupVitest  setupTests  test-setup  jest-setup
       jest-resolver  testUtils  vitest.workspace  vitest.config  vitest.setup
   (d) test directory segments: __tests__/  __mocks__/  __fixtures__/  __snapshots__/  test/  tests/
       e2e/  playwright/  vitest-mocks/
   (e) the dedicated test-infrastructure package: packages/testing/**
   (ext in: ts tsx js jsx mjs cjs).  NOTE product code whose NAME merely contains "test"/"spec"
   (e.g. SpeculationRules.tsx, TestForm.tsx, testCall.handler.ts, testTrigger.handler.ts,
   Stub*BillingRepository.ts) is intentionally NOT excluded - it is production code.

count legend:
   files   : number of DISTINCT first-party NON-TEST files containing the pattern. This is the headline
             recall metric and is directly comparable to the audit's measured file-counts (AAP 0.3.2).
   matches : total file:line:snippet evidence lines listed in the category block (>= files; one source
             line may contain several controls, one file may contain many lines).
   count   : == files (the mandated per-category terminator; equals the headline file-count metric).

CENTRALIZED-NOT-ABSENT NOTE (applies to category 8 Output Sanitization and category 9 Security Headers):
   These two controls are CENTRALIZED, NOT ABSENT. The authoritative enforcement points live in a small
   number of shared loci - e.g. apps/web/lib/csp.ts (per-request CSP nonce + 'strict-dynamic'), the edge
   proxy, and a shared DOMPurify/escape wrapper - rather than being repeated at every call site. The broad
   grep patterns below ALSO surface incidental references (helpers, comments, prop names, re-exports), so a
   raw match/file count OVER-states the number of distinct enforcement points. Therefore Layer 3b MUST
   verify that the centralized control is actually ON a given dataflow path BEFORE treating a related sink
   finding as gateBlocking. Do NOT over-block on categories 8 and 9 purely from these counts.

MULTI-LANGUAGE NOTE:
   The codebase is TypeScript/JavaScript. Python / Go / Java mitigation patterns are structurally expected
   to be EMPTY for this repository; that emptiness is NOT a failure and does NOT trigger an ERROR verdict.

NO-SILENT-FAILURE NOTE:
   All 9 categories are emitted unconditionally with an explicit count (a count of 0 is reported with the
   category header retained, never silently dropped). Severity vocabulary elsewhere in the audit normalizes
   to: critical | high | medium | low.
file-universe : total=7439  non-test=6374  test=1065  (test routed to mitigation-inventory-test.txt)
